title: Tastebuds: the editor field, a first install

fields.title: The editor field: a first install
fields.subtitle: From an empty folder to a working field

beats.say: The notes in Tastebuds are written in a small editor field. Any web page can embed it. This is a first install.

fields.title: Clone, install, build
fields.body: clone 0.3 s  ·  install 2.9 s  ·  build 1.4 s

beats.say: Clone the repository, install, and build the field. Measured on one machine, the three commands took under five seconds.
The page needs three things. A stylesheet.
An empty element, for the field to build in.
And one call: create editor, with that element and the text to start with.
beats.text: And one call: createEditor, with that element and the text to start with.

beats.say: Listen for change, and the page gets the new text after every edit.
beats.label: on *change*, save the text

beats.say: Here is that page. The field opens with its starting notes.
Type, and the text below follows every key.
Two stars make a word bold as you type. So does control B.
A dash and a space start a list.
What the page receives is plain text: a small subset of Markdown, easy to read and easy to store.
beats.label: stored as _plain text_

fields.title: One call in, one call out
fields.subtitle: createEditor · on change · destroy

beats.say: Create editor makes the field. Destroy removes it. The guide has the rest.
beats.text: createEditor makes the field. destroy removes it. The guide has the rest.
